bibliography_candidates.relevance: Relevant proof-technology source for nested and tree allocation algorithms; may help map the unequal-low reduced LP to a known nested allocation or greedy/scaling framework.
bibliography_candidates.title: Lower and Upper Bounds for the Allocation Problem and Other Nonlinear Optimization Problems

ideas.risks: The formula may be correct only under hidden path-feasibility inequalities; the p>q capacity split is the likeliest place for a missed boundary case.
ideas.summary: Independently audit the solver's two-low closed form. For p<q, verify the collapse to variables a=x_{0,p} and y=x_{0,q}+x_{1,q}, including capacity and nonnegativity constraints. For p>q, derive primal and dual certificates for both cases and check whether S1<=S2 and S2/h<=B0+B1 are sufficient.
ideas.title: Audit Two-Low Formula
ideas.why_promising: This is the most immediate partial result from iteration 19; turning it into an accepted lemma would give a reliable base case for arbitrary unequal-low pooling.

ideas.risks: The binary operation may be nonassociative; three-low examples may require a genuinely global LP rather than adjacent pooling.
ideas.summary: Treat the two-low formula as a candidate local merge operator for adjacent low levels. Test whether arbitrary unequal-low one-drought LPs can be solved by recursively pooling adjacent lows or segments, PAVA-style. Use the recorded three-low regression case 0,0.2,0^8,0.3,0,0.4,1 as a first stress test.
ideas.title: Two-Low Pooling Rule
ideas.why_promising: If a local merge rule exists, it could convert CL-049 from an LP theorem into a closed-form or near-closed-form algorithm.

ideas.risks: The running maxima m_{i,j} may destroy pure nestedness; the problem may be a more general covering LP rather than a standard nested resource-allocation problem.
ideas.summary: Start from the CL-049 dual with alpha_j, beta, and segment pressures psi_i. Try to transform the reduced LP into a nested resource-allocation, min-cost flow, polymatroid, or active-set problem. Identify exactly which structural property is needed for a polynomial certificate-producing algorithm.
ideas.title: Nested Allocation Map
ideas.why_promising: Even without a closed form, an exact algorithm with primal-dual certificates would be valuable and would connect the current LP to established allocation machinery.

ideas.risks: A computational suite can produce misleading patterns if it does not emit exact primal and dual certificates; floating-point LP values should not be promoted.
ideas.summary: Build an exact rational regression suite for the formal left-limit D_n LP and the CL-049 reduced LP. Include random small unequal-low droughts, duplicate lows, zero-length gaps, M>1 old highs, nonmonotone lows, and the known cases D_4=68/225 and the three-low 2.91 example.
ideas.title: Exact Regression Suite
ideas.why_promising: The project has repeatedly benefited from small counterexamples; exact certificates would quickly falsify bad pooling rules and protect future closed forms.

ideas.risks: One-drought structure may not compose; low quote mass can create high debt that interacts across later droughts in nonlocal ways.
ideas.summary: Analyze repeated droughts sharing resolving highs. Start with two one-drought gadgets separated by highs, then move to several low episodes before one final high. Track whether the high-debt term from low-mass choices is additive, reset by highs, or requires a state variable.
ideas.title: Repeated Drought Debt
ideas.why_promising: This is the local-to-global bottleneck for the two-level and finite-alphabet gluing program; CL-049 is local and explicitly should not be assumed composable.

ideas.risks: Prior attempts based on stable-high regret and raw waiting time failed; a new recursion must pass separated-block dilution tests.
ideas.summary: Return to the two-level finite-alphabet gluing problem using accepted drought identities. Seek a resolved-surplus/high-debt criterion that implies either a fixed sublinear envelope or a comparable-scale D_n lower bound. Test against h^M,0^N,l,0^L,h and separated 0^N,l,0^L,h examples.
ideas.title: Two-Level Gluing Criterion
ideas.why_promising: A successful two-level theorem would be the first real progress toward deciding whether D_n=o(n) can imply anytime learnability under market-specific structure.

ideas.risks: May become tautological if it merely restates the fixed-envelope criterion; needs a usable conditional or computable sufficient condition.
ideas.summary: Extend the finite-prefix LP viewpoint to stochastic exogenous processes by conditioning on histories and weighting rare hard branches. Use rare multi-threshold blocks to separate essential-sup tail failures from expected decision loss.
ideas.title: Probability-Weighted Prefix Conflict
ideas.why_promising: It connects the accepted deterministic LP machinery with the original tail-condition motivation while respecting the counterexamples based on rare or predictable delays.
